title: How to Judge a Scientific Study
subject: science

sections.body: Questions to ask: How big was the sample? Was there a CONTROL group? Were participants randomly assigned? Was it BLINDED (people didn't know who got what)?
Was it PEER-REVIEWED (checked by other experts)? Who funded it? Has it been REPLICATED by other teams?
One study is rarely the final word. Systematic reviews, which combine many studies, are stronger evidence.
Headlines often say 'X causes Y' when the study only found a correlation, or was done in mice!

quiz.q: A headline says 'Chocolate cures anxiety!' The study had 12 people and no control group. What's the best response?
hints: A survey of 5 friends isn't enough to prove a national trend. Same here.
quiz.explain: A tiny study with no control group is weak evidence; it needs much better research.

options: Neither participants nor researchers know who gets the real treatment
hints: In a taste test where neither the tasters nor the server know which cola is which, nobody's expectations sway results.
quiz.explain: In a double-blind study, neither the participants nor the researchers know who gets which treatment.
